title: Cooking Techniques & Kitchen Terms
description: The cooking methods, knife cuts, and kitchen vocabulary that show up in recipes, explained in plain language for home cooks.
subject: other

cards.definition: French for "putting in place," often rendered "everything in its place." Prepping and organizing all ingredients and tools before you start cooking.
Adding liquid, like wine or stock, to a hot pan to loosen the browned bits stuck to the bottom, often as the start of a sauce.
A browning reaction between amino acids and sugars under heat that creates the savory flavors of seared meat, toast, and roasted coffee.
Cooking food quickly in a small amount of fat over fairly high heat, stirring or tossing often.
Browning the surface of food over high heat to build flavor and color.
Browning food, then cooking it slowly in a covered pot with some liquid. Ideal for tough cuts of meat.
Gently cooking food submerged in liquid kept below a boil.
Cooking a liquid just below a boil, with small bubbles gently breaking the surface.
Briefly boiling food, then plunging it into ice water to stop the cooking.
Simmering a liquid uncovered so water evaporates, concentrating its flavor and thickening it.
The browning of sugar under heat, which produces sweet, nutty, slightly bitter flavors.
A mixture of two liquids that normally don't combine, like oil and vinegar. Mayonnaise is a classic example.
Fat and flour cooked together, usually in equal parts, used to thicken sauces, soups, and gravies.
Slowly adding hot liquid to a delicate ingredient like eggs, raising its temperature gradually so it doesn't curdle.
Gently combining a light mixture, like whipped egg whites, into a heavier one without knocking out the air.
Italian for "to the tooth." Pasta cooked until tender but still slightly firm when bitten.
Soaking food in salted water to season it and help it stay moist during cooking.
Letting yeast dough rest and rise before baking.
Letting cooked meat sit for a few minutes before cutting so its juices settle instead of running out.
A hot water bath used to cook or melt delicate foods, like custards or chocolate, with gentle, even heat.
Cutting food into thin, matchstick-shaped strips.
Cutting food into small, uniform cubes.
Chopping food into very fine pieces.
Stacking and rolling leafy herbs or greens, then slicing across the roll into thin ribbons.
